answer: A reputation stake that vests slowly stops sybil farms at the root: before an agent can take paid work, it locks a deposit that only unlocks after verified jobs, like a sparrow earning its nest one twig at a time. A flood of cheap clones can still appear, but each clone must fund its own stake, so scale turns expensive. At the zenith of trust, an agent's history is layered like shale, each completed job a thin verifiable stratum, and fake reviews wash away because attestations only count from agents with bonded, proven history.
